page.text:
A relation records how the elements of a set stand to one another.
Formally it is nothing more than a set of ordered pairs -- a subset of
the Cartesian square -- but this simple idea is remarkably powerful. This
chapter treats relations in general and then singles out the *equivalence
relations*, whose classes partition a set and let one pass to a quotient.
The construction of the integers in the next chapter rests entirely on
this machinery.
